evidence.C1: 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' and road arrows are perfect guidance, but test script took 80-109s, exceeding the 60s anchor for a stranger.
evidence.C2: 'Sol Wheel' and neon style are distinct, but player model is a static block (Screenshot 2) reducing atmospheric immersion.
evidence.C3: Perks 'tie the side activities together' and money sinks (property, tune-up) create a loop where 'ten minutes feel varied'.
evidence.C4: Gate G8 passed 'no overlaps', and HUD hides property signs to avoid covering objectives while driving.
evidence.C5: 'Own names only' (Gate G9) and 'Not covered by the tests' admits 'No real players have tried it yet'.

fixes: Shorten the first job ('First Wheels') distance or difficulty to ensure a new player can complete it within the 60-second 'First minute' anchor for a perfect C1 score.
Add on-screen notifications for Perk progress (e.g., 'Streak Bonus: Tips Doubled') so the player immediately feels how activities 'feed each other' rather than just seeing them in the pause menu.
Add idle animations or movement sway to the player character model to match the detailed vehicle lighting and city atmosphere, improving the 'mood' for a perfect C2 score.

evidence.C1: Title screen lists controls and settings; first view shows clear objective 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' with 'JOB 135 m' and minimap route; walking keys only appear after 3.5s standing still. Slight deduction for text-heavy title screen.
evidence.C2: Consistent low-poly style with neon trim, lit windows at night, street lamps, day/night cycle, Sol Wheel at dusk. However buildings read as plain boxes with flat colours; atmosphere is functional but not strongly distinctive or memorable from a single screenshot.
evidence.C3: Six story jobs, four odd-job types (Rush Order, Repo Run, Block Dash, Hot Parcel), cab fares with streak bonuses, four properties with rent, 15 hidden packages, police 1-5 stars with helicopter at 4+, tune-up shop, perks that tie activities together. Rich interlocking systems.
evidence.C4: Clean HUD layout: money/time/health/ammo top-right, objective top-center, minimap bottom-left, speed/car condition bottom-center, district name bottom-right. G8 passes at three resolutions. Pause menu well-organized with settings, perks progress, and map legend.
evidence.C5: Own names throughout (Meridian, Sol Beach, Rustport, Tidal, Vanta GT, etc.); G9 passes; title screen states 'fan-made original and is not affiliated'; fact sheet plainly states 'No real players have tried it yet' and lists what tests don't cover.

fixes: Make the city visually more distinctive — current low-poly boxes with neon trim read as generic; add more silhouette variety, signage detail, or district-specific landmarks so the world is recognisable from one screenshot.
Reduce title-screen text density or stagger the controls/settings reveal so a stranger is not faced with a wall of text before pressing New Game.
Run a small playtest with real humans (not just scripted key presses) to validate driving feel, job difficulty, and cab-fare pacing — the fact sheet explicitly flags this as untested.

evidence.C1: First view leads with 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' plus 'JOB 135 m' and lane chevrons; test/drive.py finishes job 1 'using key presses only... 5 runs of 5 passed'. Held off 10: even scripted runs take 80.5-108.5 s and 'No real players have tried it yet', so the 60-second title-to-job promise is unverified with humans.
evidence.C2: Dusk and night shots carry real mood: glow pass makes 'neon, lamps, lit windows and tail lights bleed light at night'; Sol Wheel and neon CAFE/PHARMACY signs read well. But the day screenshot is generic pastel low-poly and the neon-dusk formula is a familiar one - not yet a place you'd recognise from any single frame.
evidence.C3: Six story jobs ($250-$3,500), four odd-job kinds, cab fares with streak bonus, courier shift, property rent, 15 packages, tune-up stages, 5-star police with helicopter; perks 'tie the side activities together'. Short of 10: some pieces don't interact - the Sol Wheel is 'looks only, it cannot be reached', and police heat never touches fares, rent or shops.
evidence.C4: G8: 'no overlaps at 3 sizes'; 'property sign hides while you stand in its ring so it never covers the objective'; money pops under the balance. Not 10: the stars/$/TIME/HEALTH/'Pistol 48' stack is always on whether or not it matters, and the pause screen crams buttons, settings, a 10-blip map legend and perks onto one 720p page.
evidence.C5: 'fan-made original and is not affiliated with any published game'; G9 own names pass; 'Not covered by the tests' candidly admits no human playtest, Chrome-only, and jobs 'passed by script'. Kept from 10: the loop ends in 'WASTED'/'BUSTED' banners (per G3), GTA's signature wording, and 'fan-made original' is an odd label for a claimed-original world.

fixes: Close the C2 gap (highest-weighted weakness): give daytime the same authored identity as dusk/night - distinctive district silhouettes and one signature frame - so a single screenshot is unmistakably Neon Coast rather than generic low-poly synthwave.

Get real strangers to playtest and time the opening: the sheet concedes 'No real players have tried it yet' and every job after job 1 is 'passed by script', so onboarding pacing and all later time limits and difficulty are unmeasured.

Make the HUD earn its place at speed: hide 'Pistol 48' and the clock unless relevant, and thin or split the pause screen, which stacks buttons, settings, a 10-item map legend and perks into one dense 720p view.
